newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end lower, affected by Jinro troubles.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end lower, affected by Jinro troubles.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed slightly lower on Tuesday in slow trading as news of Jinro Ltd's loan default kept most investors at bay, brokers said.
But they said foreign buying, focused on shares deemed to be undervalued, limited the market's steep slide.
The composite index ended 1.24 points lower at 732.68.
"The Jinro trouble was definitely bad news. But investors refrained from dumping shares because of the view the market was oversold," said Park Young-shik of Daewoo Securities.
Brokers forecast similar trading patterns on Wednesday.
Jinro Ltd failed to repay the loans on Monday and faced a second deadline on Tuesday to avoid final default, which would have triggered court-receivership proceedings.
But unlisted Donghwa Leasing Co Ltd, which now holds about eight billion won worth of Jinro's promissory notes, said on Tuesday it would extend repayment of the notes to next February.
"But the extension of the loan repayment is not a permanent solution to Jinro's problems," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
POSCO fell 1,700 won to 58,900 after the company said it would offer to buy part of the troubled Hanbo Steel Co's assets.
Brokers said the purchase of Hanbo's assets would be a financial burden to POSCO.
A POSCO executive said on Tuesday he estimated the price for Hanbo's fixed assets at about two trillion won.

Hanbo's creditors called a second auction on Tuesday to sell off Hanbo Steel which collapsed in January under debts of about five trillion won. But Hanbo's main creditor Korea First Bank said it had received no bids except POSCO's offer.
Shares of the Jinro Group's two listed firms dropped by their daily limit on news that Jinro Ltd had failed to honour repayments of eight billion won of promissory notes on Monday.
Jinro Ind. fell 400 won to its daily lower limit of 4,620, while Jinro General Foods dropped 300 won to its limit of 3,560.
Trading of Jinro Ltd was suspended for today because of the default.
Brokers said LG Group companies, including LG Electronics and LG Semicon, were in demand by foreign investors.
Foreigners bought about 150,000 shares of LG Electronics, which lost 200 won to 18,400 and about 100,000 shares of LG Semicon, which remained flat at 44,200.
They also purchased 200,000 shares of Daewoo Heavy, which rose 40 won to 7,700 and 100,000 shares of KEPCO, which gained 200 won to 27,000.
